etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English, borrowed from Old French superiour, from Latin superior (“higher, upper”).

definitions.definition: Of high standard or quality.

quote.citation: 1905, E. M. Forster, Where Angels Fear to Tread , chapter 3:
quote.text: She always treated (her husband) as a boy, which he was, and as a fool, which he was not, thinking herself so immeasurably superior to him that she neglected opportunity after opportunity of establishing her rule.

definitions.definition: Greater in size or power.
(superior to) Beyond the power or influence of; too great or firm to be subdued or affected by.

quote.citation: 1711 December 12 (Gregorian calendar), [Joseph Addison; Richard Steele et al.], “SATURDAY, December 1, 1711”, in The Spectator, number 237; republished in Alexander Chalmers, editor, The Spectator; a New Edition, […], volume III, New York, N.Y.: D[aniel] Appleton & Company, 1853, →OCLC:
quote.text: There is not in earth a spectacle more worthy  […] than a brave man superior to his sufferings.The spelling has been modernized.

definitions.definition: Greater or better than average.
Higher in rank, status, or quality.

quote.citation: 1918, W[illiam] B[abington] Maxwell, chapter XII, in The Mirror and the Lamp, Indianapolis, Ind.: The Bobbs-Merrill Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: There were many wooden chairs for the bulk of his visitors, and two wicker armchairs with red cloth cushions for superior people. From the packing-cases had emerged some Indian clubs, […], and all these articles […] made a scattered and untidy decoration that Mrs. Clough assiduously dusted and greatly cherished.

quote.citation: 2022 January 12, David Clough, “From Germany with love: a Warship perspective”, in RAIL, number 948, page 46:
quote.text: Additionally, reliability proved to be superior to NBL's design, with an average of 120,000 miles run during 1959.

definitions.definition: Courageously or serenely indifferent (as to something painful or disheartening).
(typography) Printed in superscript.
(anatomy, medicine) Located above or higher, a direction that in humans corresponds to cephalad.
(botany) (of a calyx) Above the ovary; said of parts of the flower which, although normally below the ovary, adhere to it, and so appear to originate from its upper part.
(botany) (of an ovary) Above and free from the other floral organs.
(botany) Belonging to the part of an axillary flower which is toward the main stem.
(botany) (of the radicle) Pointing toward the apex of the fruit.
Located above or out; higher in position.
(taxonomy) More comprehensive.
Affecting or assuming an air of superiority.
(astronomy, of a planet in the Solar System) Having a wider orbit around the Sun; typically with respect to the Earth.
The senior person in a monastic community.
The head of certain religious institutions and colleges.
A person of higher rank or quality, especially a colleague in a higher position.
(printing) A superior letter, figure, or symbol.
(Scots law, historical) One who has made an original grant of heritable property to a tenant or vassal, on condition of a certain annual payment (feu duty) or of the performance of certain services.
